title: What happens when the test set leaks in?
description: Course activity for Exercise 10: compare a correct pipeline (preprocessing fit on training rows only) against a leaky variant (the same step fit on training and test rows together) for scaling, feature selection, and PCA, on real ABIDE-II participants predicting age from cortical thickness.
instructions: Choose a preprocessing operation, a sample size, and one of five predetermined split seeds. Both pipelines use the exact same participants and the exact same training/test split -- only whether the operation saw the test rows differs.
reflectionPrompts: Which participants influenced this preprocessing step in the leaky version?
Why is target-informed feature selection a more direct form of leakage than scaling?
If the correct and leaky scores are almost equal for your chosen split, does that make the leaky procedure valid?
Why can small samples make this comparison more unstable from one split to the next?
